description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p20-readline.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 3 rows):
  readline.t 28 `tell returns -1 after last gv is unglobbed`
  readline.t 29 `unglobbery of last gv nullifies PL_last_in_gv`
  readline.t 30 `readline *$glob_copy sets PL_last_in_gv`
  -- perl-tests/readline.t:265-276 ([perl #97988])

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    open *foom, '<', $0 or die;
    my %f; $f{g} = *foom;
    readline $f{g};
    $f{g} = 3;                       # the last glob copy is gone
    print "28 tell = ", tell, "\n";
    $f{g} = *foom;                   # must have no effect
    print "29 tell = ", tell, "\n";
    readline *{$f{g}};
    print "30 tell = ", tell, " vs tell *foom = ", tell(*foom), "\n";
  perl: 28 -1   29 -1   30 37 vs 37
  PCL : 28 0    29 0    30 0  vs -1

TWO MISSES IN ONE MECHANISM:
  (a) argument-less `tell` returns 0 unconditionally -- there is no
      last-read-handle state (perl's `PL_last_in_gv`), so rows 28/29 read 0
      where perl reads -1 and row 30 reads 0 where perl reads the position.
  (b) `tell(*foom)` on an OPEN handle that has been read from returns -1 --
      so the explicit-argument spelling is wrong too, in the opposite
      direction, for a handle named by a GLOB.
Fix area: `p-tell` in `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` plus a `*p-last-read-handle*`
set by `p-readline` and cleared when the glob holding it is overwritten.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md readline.t, "`tell()` after
GV unglobbed (tests 28-30): `tell()` should return -1 after the last typeglob
pointing to a filehandle is destroyed.  PCL returns 0."  Shape (b) is new.
subject: BUG (tell): PCL tracks no "last handle read from", so argument-less `tell` always returns 0 -- perl returns the position of the last handle read, and -1 once that handle has been unglobbed
